script.cite: BK4 printed pp.84-85 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF pp.90-91 (decoding rule and procedure, image-read); derived from topology and the p.85 rule, not printed: p.84-85 tie no lamp to a bit weight (O-C19), the weights come from the wiring (light 3 = 8, 4 = 4, 5 = 2, 6 = 1), the same order Book IV prints on p.77 (PDF p.83) for lights 3-6; hand at pad N puts + (D16/M+) on DN; position 1: D1/6com feeds lamp 6 (6A, lamp, 6B/6-) direct; no coil pad, lights 3-6 read 0001 = 1; every relay arm (1H-1L-2L-2H-3H-3L-4L-4H-5H-5L-6L-6H) is strapped to + by 6H/6+, and every coil F end is chained 1F..6F/6- to minus; lamps 1 and 2 and every nC are unwired, so output lamps 1-2 and all indicator lamps stay dark; no contact feeds a coil except 3G/6E, so nothing latches and every relay not named is released (nc)
script.quote: In this method, the computer is programmed to recognize a decimal number by the location of the input pulse; a series of direct contacts then convert this pulse to the appropriate binary number. The following program mechanizes such a method. Setting the rotary switch to any number from 0 through 10 will cause the equivalent binary number to appear in the output lights. [...] Enter any decimal number from 0 through 10 by turning the rotary switch to the desired position. The binary equivalent of the decimal number will appear in the binary output lights. (A light ON represents 1; a light OFF represents 0.)

note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the 49-wire topology and the p.84-85 decoding rule, not printed. No erratum touches Book IV pp.84-85. Topology: the wiper D16 is strapped to M+; pads D1, D2, D4 and D8 feed lamp nodes 6com, 5com, 4com and 3com (lights 6, 5, 4, 3) direct; pads D3, D5, D6, D7, D9 and D10 pull relays 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1, whose N.O. contacts (G and K, arms all on +) put + on two lamp nodes each, and relay 3 also pulls relay 6 through 3G/6E. The decoded pattern is the binary of the pad number with light 3 = 8 and light 6 = 1 (O-C19 asks whether that order counts as printed). Script choices, not printed: positions 1-10 are entered in order by hand, one pad per grab, each held 1000 ms (hand_slew_mrpm 30 rpm crosses 22.5 deg in about 125 ms); the final return to 0 goes by the shortest path over unwired pads 11-15 and dwells 3000 ms so lamps cool before the check that every relay has released. Construction state is dial on D0, restated by the first dialGrab.
